### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **46** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-storage/README.md`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**57** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-storage/README.md`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `35e85c0824c4e910e1e037261a62ca069be01426` — the merge of head `cb31937dcc5e30cb340f9bb565236a87d0c5da1b` into base `3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 35e85c0824c4e910e1e037261a62ca069be01426 && git checkout 35e85c0824c4e910e1e037261a62ca069be01426
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db cb31937dcc5e30cb340f9bb565236a87d0c5da1b && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db && git merge --no-ff cb31937dcc5e30cb340f9bb565236a87d0c5da1b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cb31937dcc5e30cb340f9bb565236a87d0c5da1b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/storage.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/upload-ownership.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/apps/console/src/App.tsx

Read at 2026-11-07T03:35Z: the PR body as rewritten, its 26-file list, the three-dot diff against the merge base `5210acfbae` (`origin/main` has since moved two commits, to `0f920b941f`, touching none of the PR's 26 paths), the check-runs on this head, and the cited code on `main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on this head.** All ten required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. Check Changeset went red on its first run (2026-11-07T02:35:19Z) because the body then read `Metadata-protocol: none` while the diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`; the re-run after the body edit (2026-11-07T03:26:45Z) is `success`, as is the re-run of the PR-body guards. Dogfood Regression Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI and UI Published Artifacts are `skipped` on this PR run as the two-speed battery declares. Nothing is still running.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set moves in two published places and one door. Each change, judged:

1. **`CompleteUploadRequestSchema.attachTo`** — optional `{ parentObject, parentId }`, both non-empty strings. Right. The door reads it through a closed set (`attachTargetOf`): an array, `null`, a non-object, an empty string or any key outside the two declared is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST` before the file row is read, so a malformed target learns nothing about any file. Pinned at the door for five malformed shapes with the attacher never called.

2. **`FileUploadResponseSchema.data.attachmentId`** — optional, present only when the request carried `attachTo`. Right. A completion without `attachTo` answers exactly the prior shape through the same `committedFileMetadata` projection; pinned.

3. **The door's attach arm, and its order.** The gates the door already asked run first and unchanged: session (401), `fileId` (400), target shape (400), the row (404), the uploader rule (403), the starting organization (409), the held bytes (409). Only then is the attacher asked, and only in a mount that bound one; the public registrar and the open mode (`session === null`) answer `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and commit nothing. Right: a request refused by any prior gate never reaches the verb (pinned for 401, 403, 404, 409 and the five 400s), and the no-attacher mount keeps the plain commit unchanged.

4. **The verb's premise, re-asked inside the verb.** `attachUploadAs` reads the row as the system by id and asks, in order: `isFileUploader` (an empty owner, another owner and no row all take the uploader rule's one answer), `status === 'pending'`, `scope === 'attachments'`, `organizationOutOfWriteReach` against the caller's active organization, `findFileHolder` (a `sys_attachment` row naming the file, or the row's own `ref_*` columns), `heldBytesRefusal`. Right, and each is the existing definition, not a copy: the uploader rule is the commit door's, the holder question is the reap guard's, the bytes question is the commit door's own. So the set of files the vouch can ever name is: a row the caller's own presign created in the attachments scope, still pending, held by nothing, with bytes present, in the caller's write reach. A row the system `attachFile` created has no owner and is refused; a row `attachFileAs` created is committed and is refused; a `user`-scope upload is refused.

5. **The parent authorization, before any write.** `assertMayAttach` asks the security service's `explain` for `sys_attachment` create and the parent-EDIT attach rule with the parent read as the caller; `organizationOfParent` reads the parent as the caller again and refuses a parent that does not exist, that the caller cannot read, or that is walled into another organization with one answer; then the file's organization must equal the organization the attachment is written in. Right. The insert itself runs as the caller, so the engine's own gates judge the caller too: `enable.files` (pinned `FILES_DISABLED`), the attach-rule hook, the `uploaded_by` stamp, RLS and FLS. The row's `file_name`, `mime_type` and `size` come from the `sys_file` row the verb read, never from the request.

6. **What the vouch admits.** One `(sys_attachment, file_id, file.id)` triple, on the verb's own insert; the existence probe still runs. Right, and unchanged from the mark's published contract: `vouchForReference` and `isVouchedReference` keep their signatures, and the reference check's one consultation of the mark is untouched. The generic data door carries no mark; pinned twice — a unit case where the same member's direct insert naming the file the verb just committed is refused `reference_not_found`, and the dogfood's two-step control.

7. **The one-shot strip.** `withoutVouchedReferences` runs where `buildHookApi` builds every hook's api, so `ctx.api`, `withRunAs('user')` and `sudo` all derive from a context without the mark. Right. Pinned in objectql both ways: a hook naming the vouched id again through either api is refused, and the same hook under an unmarked system write lands (so the refusal is the mark being spent, not the hook failing). The strip is own-property based; the mark is set only by spread, so there is no inherited-property shape for it to miss in the engine (no `Object.create` of a context anywhere in objectql's source).

8. **Error paths.** The insert and the commit run in one `inOneUnit`: an owned transaction rolls both back; a unit the call does not own removes the inserted row best-effort and logs the row id when it cannot. The upload itself is never touched by a refusal: it stays `pending`, bytes stored, attached to nothing, and the pending-upload retention reclaims it. Right. The door relays a declared 4xx with its code, status, message and details, a declared 5xx with its code and status and generic text, and anything undeclared as a generic 500; pinned for all three.

9. **Disclosure.** For a file that is not the caller's upload, the only answers the door ever gives are its pre-existing `404 FILE_NOT_FOUND` and `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, both before any fact about the row; every 409 and 400 that describes a file's state is reached only by its uploader. The verb's own answer for another user's row and for no row is one body (pinned byte-equal). Right; see ③ for the door's two codes.

10. **Console.** The panel sends `attachTo` with the completion and makes no second call; a 200 without an `attachmentId` is an error, never a silent success; the adapter puts the server's `code` and `status` on the thrown error so the panel maps refusals without parsing text; `uploaded_by` is no longer sent (the server stamps it). Right. The write census drops the panel's `create` site and keeps its `delete` site; the `attachmentUpload` affordance row is still read where Upload is offered.

11. **Counts.** The tenant audit census moves 265 to 266 for the verb's new insert; the strictness ledger moves api 500 to 501 for the new `attachTo` object; the authorable-surface shard gains `api/CompleteUploadRequest:attachTo`; the generated storage reference carries the new key, its nested shape and the response field. Mechanical and consistent with the diff.

Two things the rule leaves open, neither a widening of any caller's rights:

- **(should-fix) The commit is not conditional on the state the verb read.** The pending and unheld checks are reads, and the commit writes `status: 'committed'` by id without a `where status = 'pending'` arm. Two completions of the same upload racing through the arm can each write a `sys_attachment` row for the caller's own file on parents the caller may attach to. Every row so written is one the caller is entitled to create, and the surface already admits one file on more than one record, so the accept set does not grow; but the invariant the header states ("held by nothing") is held by a read. The fix is one condition on the commit (or refusing when `updateFile` reports the state moved), answered `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.

- **(should-fix) The mark still rides `ctx.input.options.context`.** The engine builds each insert hook's `input.options` from the operation's options, whose `context` is the vouched one, so a platform hook that forwards `ctx.input.options` into a nested write carries the mark. It is admitted only for the same triple, which the verb has already judged, and no platform hook on `sys_attachment` forwards its options today (the lifecycle hooks write `sys_file` under their own system context). But the module header now says "no hook inherits it", which is wider than the code: either strip at the hook's options view too, or narrow the sentence to the api. The dev flagged this one.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right. One optional request key and one optional response field enter; nothing is removed, refused or re-meant.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` — right. The authorable-surface shard moves by one added key, which is what the gate reads; the first Check Changeset run was red on `none`, and the body and changeset now both read `added`, re-run green.
- Levels: `@objectstack/spec` minor; `core`, `objectql`, `service-storage`, `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch — right under the kind-decides-the-level rule. No BREAKING banner is owed and none is written; no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- `Skills-docs: updated here` — right. `skills/` and `.claude/skills/` on `main` carry no `upload/complete`, `CompleteUploadRequest` or `attachTo`; the two hand-written docs state the key and its refusals; the route ledger and the service README say what the door now does; the generated reference is regenerated.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The door answers 404 for an id that names no file and 403 for another user's id.** Pre-existing: the commit door's `getFile` 404 has preceded the uploader rule since that rule landed, on completion with or without `attachTo`, and the two chunked doors do the same. The verb's own answer is one body for both. Ids are server-minted random UUIDs. Judgment: follow-up — a card on the three upload doors to give the uploader rule's one body for a missing row too, as the rule's own text already says; not this PR's to change, and the doc table here states both codes honestly.
2. **A platform hook forwarding `ctx.input.options` into a nested write carries the vouched context.** Judgment: should-fix (①, second open item). Admitted only for the triple the verb judged; the fix is a strip at the options view or a narrower header sentence.
3. **Concurrent completions of one upload through the arm.** Judgment: should-fix (①, first open item). No rights gained; the state invariant should be a write condition.
4. **Version skew between console and server.** A panel carrying `attachTo` against a server without the arm gets a 200 with no `attachmentId`; the panel reports it as an error, and the server has committed an unattached file. Judgment: follow-up note only — the console and the server ship from one tree, and the panel's answer is loud.

### ④ Design judgment

**The seam.** Putting the attach on the complete door is the right seam, and the body's three reasons hold against the code: `pending` plus the uploader rule is exactly the proof the vouch rests on, and a separate attach route after a commit would have to vouch for a committed file a member cannot read, a wider premise; the commit and the row are one unit, so no committed-but-unattached file is left for a refused attach; and the panel loses a round trip rather than gaining a route. Route ownership holds: one route, one owner, the attacher a parameter of `registerStorageFamily` bound only by `composeStorageRoutes`, so no host hands the door an attacher of its own, and the public registrar refuses loudly (501) rather than serving a bare miss. The one tension is that the arm resolves the request's full execution context a second time after `requireUploadSession` has already resolved a session; the verb needs the full context (RLS, sharing, grants) and the door's session gate predates it, so both are correct, and a single resolution is a tidy-up for later, not a defect.

**The mark.** The PR reuses the one-file vouch without widening it: no new signature, no new field on the context, one new call site vouching the same triple on the same kind of insert (the caller's own `sys_attachment` row for a file the same call authorized), and the existence probe untouched. `withoutVouchedReferences` narrows the mark's reach rather than widens it, and the module header is rewritten to say so; the census gate that pins the mark's call sites moved to its own Tier H PR because of its workflow step, which is the right split — this PR touches no governed path (0 of 26 against the register).

**Consumer hunt — every caller of the complete door and every reader of its answer, on `main`:**

- `packages/client/src/index.ts` `storage.upload` — sends `{ fileId, eTag }`, never `attachTo`, and reads `FileUploadResponse`; the optional field is absent for it. Unchanged.
- CLI — no caller of the door. MCP — no attach tool and no caller. Unchanged.
- Console: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx` is now the one sender of `attachTo`; `ui/apps/console/src/App.tsx` builds the same adapter for file fields without `attachTo`, so its completion body stays `{ fileId }` and the response body is not read. The adapter's thrown error gains `status` and `code` (additive; the message text is unchanged). The `currentUserId` prop stays on the panel's interface, so a host passing it still compiles.
- Tests on `main` that call the door without `attachTo`: dogfood `anonymous-door-sweep`, `attachments-permission-matrix`, `cbp-parent-attachment-comment-gates`, `field-file-collection`, `field-zoo-roundtrip`, `file-field-hydration-no-denial`, `fixtures/attachments-authz-harness`, `flow-screen-file-intake`, `predicate-write-unreadable-not-matched`, `storage-unclaimed-download`, `write-door-unreadable-is-not-found`; organizations `storage-upload-door-ownership.wall` and `storage-upload-organization-change.wall`. Their request and answer shapes are unchanged.
- Readers of an `attachmentId`: the print service answers its own `{ fileId, attachmentId }` from `attachFileAs`, a different surface; unchanged.
- Docs naming the door: `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`, the service README and the route ledger are updated in the diff; `content/docs/references/api/storage.mdx` is regenerated.

Nothing breaks; the one behaviour change for an existing caller is the panel's, which is the fix.
